$comment: AES interop vectors produced by the Java Pesepay server's own cipher path.
Generated by scripts/java/GenerateVectors.java, which mirrors PaymentPayloadEncryptionHelper.
DO NOT regenerate these from the Node implementation: they exist to prove Node agrees with Java.

algorithm.keyDerivation: SecretKeySpec over the key's UTF-8 bytes (32 chars => 32 bytes => AES-256)
algorithm.ivDerivation: key.substring(0, 16) as UTF-8 bytes - a CHAR slice, hence the ASCII requirement
algorithm.padding: PKCS#5 == PKCS#7 at a 16-byte block size
algorithm.encoding: standard base64 with padding, not base64url

vectors.name: empty-string
vectors.note: Zero-length input still produces one full block of PKCS#7 padding.

vectors.name: single-byte
vectors.note: Shortest non-empty input; 15 bytes of padding.

vectors.name: block-minus-one
vectors.note: 15 bytes: a single padding byte, the tightest fit.

vectors.name: exact-one-block
vectors.note: Exactly 16 bytes. PKCS#7 must append a WHOLE extra block, so an implementation that pads only on a remainder yields 16 bytes here, not 32.

vectors.name: exact-two-blocks
vectors.note: Exactly 32 bytes - the same full-padding-block trap one block further out.

vectors.name: initiate-transaction-request
vectors.note: A real /v1/payments/initiate request body as the SDK serialises it.

vectors.name: payment-transaction-result
vectors.note: A real decrypted PaymentTransactionResult, carrying the transactionStatus the SDK surfaces.

vectors.name: non-ascii-plaintext
vectors.note: Multi-byte UTF-8 in the PLAINTEXT is fine; only the KEY must be ASCII, because Java derives the IV by chars and Node by bytes.

vectors.name: second-key
vectors.note: Identical plaintext under a different key, so a hardcoded key or IV cannot pass.

vectors.name: large-payload
vectors.note: 2 KiB of metadata, well past a single cipher update.
